scores.note: Reactors and weapons reached many societies as a new energy source, and nuclear physics, power, medicine and strategy all grew from it.
Atoms with weights became the basis of chemical reasoning for chemists everywhere, and quantitative chemistry and the fields built on it rest on it.
One textbook's adoption of an existing scale gave physiological chemists a clearer measure with few direct successors, which scores below the reviewed tier 1.
It reorganised chemistry for chemists and many later fields rest on it, but reach beyond the science is indirect, so the total falls short of tier 0.
One inconclusive buoy survey by a single research team changed no practice and nothing later is known to rest on it.
One experiment linked electricity and magnetism, and needle telegraphs, electromagnets, motors and field theory embody it directly, which scores above the reviewed tier 1.
A prize question from one academy changed nothing by itself and led to one line of experiment, which scores below the reviewed tier 2.
It changed what light and electricity were taken to be, and radio, electrical engineering and later physics across many societies rest on it.
The apparatus first made fast electrical oscillations producible and detectable, and spark wireless grew from it, which scores above the reviewed tier 2.
One bench demonstration first turned current into continuous motion for experimenters, and the line of electric motors followed from it.
A second, clearer demonstration of induction already found, known to physicists, from which magneto-electric machines followed.
One experiment extended the new electromagnetism to forces between currents for physicists, and electrodynamics as a line of work grew from it.
It showed physicists that electrical waves travel in air, but later radio rested more on the oscillator, so it scores below the reviewed tier 1.
One apparatus first drew steady current from motion for experimenters, and the line of electrical generators followed from that demonstration.
One experiment revealed induction, and transformers, generators and electrical power that many societies came to live with all rest directly on it.
It gave engineers and physicists a new limit on engine work and thermodynamics grew from it, but with reach of one profession it falls short of tier 0.
A clearer mathematical restatement of Carnot for physicists through which later thermodynamics passed, which as a restatement scores below the reviewed tier 1.
It joined two existing results into the working basis of thermodynamics for physicists and engineers, and many fields built on it, but the total falls short of tier 0.
The first measured link between work and heat gave physicists a new quantity, and the work of Clausius, Thomson and Joule himself built on it.
The exact value made physicists rebuild heat theory around equivalence, but the platform credit belongs to the wider principle, so it scores below tier 0.
One laboratory's rebuilt apparatus that made a first estimate possible, with one direct successor, which scores just below the reviewed tier 2.
The first configuration of one laboratory's apparatus gave no result by itself and was succeeded only by its own revision.
More exact steam data for engineers and physicists that the thermodynamic papers drew on, which as a refinement scores below the reviewed tier 1.
One paper gave physicists worked numbers for an existing theory and fed two direct successors.
A full restatement of heat-engine theory on equivalence for physicists and engineers, from which engineering thermodynamics developed as a line of work.
Used by physicists and astronomers, it changed what space, time and gravity are taken to be, and cosmology and relativistic astrophysics rest on it.
It united earthly and heavenly motion, changing the picture of the world for the learned, and astronomy, navigation tables and later physics were built on it.
The prism trials gave natural philosophers a new account of colour, and reflecting telescopes and the study of spectra grew from them.
One experiment gave physicists the first evidence that magnetism acts on light, and magneto-optics and part of field theory grew from it.
One cast component in one workshop saved weight in an existing kind of engine, with few direct successors, which scores just below the reviewed tier 2.
It let Alpine people cross deep snow, but nothing later is known to descend from this Alpine origin, so it scores below the reviewed tier 1.
One voyage by one crew confirmed a relearned skill and was followed by a few further voyages, which scores just below the reviewed tier 2.
One copy of a known watch showed the design could be reproduced and had a few successors, which scores just below the reviewed tier 2.
A simplified copy of a known instrument carried on a few voyages, followed by one further copy.
One navigator's demonstration gave one research team working knowledge of an existing skill and one follow-up survey, which scores just below tier 2.
A new direction-finding ability that spread across many societies, on which navigation, surveying, mining and the study of magnetism rested for centuries.
One guided crossing passed existing regional pilot knowledge to a fleet from another society, with a few later passages following it.
One teaching episode gave a small group of Hawaiian voyagers an ability they lacked, with a few navigators trained in succession.
One voyage showed Hawaiian and Pacific communities that an existing skill could span long distances, with a few later voyages following.
A preparation method used by two people before one voyage, with that voyage as its only known successor.
Railways changed how many societies moved people and goods and a whole engineering field grew, but generativity of 2 leaves it one step below tier 0.
It gave Arctic peoples a new sea-hunting ability across one region, with a few later derivatives, which scores below the reviewed tier 1.
A distinct manoeuvre within existing outrigger sailing, used across one island region with few known successors, which scores below the reviewed tier 1.
One rebuilt canoe let Hawaiian voyagers test an old capability at sea, and a few later canoes and voyages followed it.
A design hypothesis by two people for one vessel, with that vessel as its only successor.
One short-lived experimental boat that failed at sea and had one successor, which scores below the reviewed tier 2.
Gunpowder weapons reached most regions and reorganised warfare, and firearms, artillery, blasting, rocketry and fireworks were built on it over centuries.
A secret machine gave one codebreaking centre a new electronic ability, with little passed on openly, so it scores below the reviewed tier 1.
A single specimen showing an existing joining technique, with nothing later known to rest on it.
